narrative:
The model estimates a 48% chance that you will leave your job, which is high enough for the company to deny your promotion as a precaution.

Three main factors shaped this outlook. First, the model noted that you have not received any other job offers while working here. This lack of external opportunities is the strongest reason the system leaned toward predicting you might stay. Second, your overall career experience of 6 to 10 years pushes the prediction in the opposite direction. Most employees the model expects to stay have only 1 to 5 years of total experience, so your longer background makes the system think you are more likely to explore new options. Third, having spent 1 to 5 years in your current role also pulls the prediction toward leaving. This tenure is typical for people the model flags as flight risks, unlike the longer stays seen in those predicted to remain.

Taken together, your solid experience and time already invested here outweighed the stabilizing effect of having no outside offers, tipping the balance just enough for the system to expect you might depart.

The company should talk with you openly about your career goals and what would make you want to grow here long-term. You might consider what would increase your sense of opportunity inside the organization so future promotion decisions can be based on clearer signals of commitment.
